body: Karvy Stock Broking (unlisted, one of India's largest retail brokers) used clients' power-of-attorney to pledge their securities (reported ~Rs 2,300-2,700 cr of client shares, >95,000 clients) with banks/NBFCs for its own loans; a net ~Rs 1,096 cr moved to group company Karvy Realty between Apr 2016 and Oct 2019. NSE's inspection led to a SEBI ex-parte order on 22 Nov 2019 barring new clients; NSDL transferred shares back to ~80,000+ clients; SEBI refused relief to lenders who had taken the pledges. NSE expelled Karvy in 2020 and SEBI later cancelled its registration; the CMD was arrested in 2021. Visible flags: (1) a broker borrowing heavily from banks against 'own' securities that were actually client holdings; (2) group diversion into real estate; (3) mismatch between client ledger balances and demat holdings (only detectable by regulators/clients via CAS). Investor-level signal: securities in your Consolidated Account Statement moving to the broker's pool account or being pledged without your consent. Outcome: SEBI tightened norms (margin pledge/re-pledge system in 2020, curbs on PoA, segregation and client-fund reporting). Lesson: custody/counterparty risk is part of portfolio risk -- reconcile the monthly CAS, avoid giving open PoA, spread holdings across brokers.

data.early_signals: broker borrowing against client securities; group transfers to realty arm

title: Karvy Stock Broking misuse of client securities (2019)
